growth_signal.value: Won a €61.6 million EuroHPC grant in 2025, said to be the largest ever EU grant to an AI semiconductor firm.

raised.note: confirmed by two sources in the run; the URLs were not saved

entry.idea: Axelera AI designs computer chips that run AI programs efficiently on devices like cameras, robots and cars, instead of sending everything to the cloud.
entry.lesson: Instead of competing head-on with a giant across all of AI computing, specialise in one part of the job and do it more efficiently.
entry.name: Axelera AI

growth.basis: substitute: a record-size grant and a bigger funding round than before
growth.reason: No revenue, customer or shipment numbers were found; the clearest recent signal is a record EU grant rather than a growth number.

market.reason: On-device AI chips could be used in almost every kind of device across many industries worldwide.

tech.reason: Designing competitive AI chips takes rare engineering skill and years of work, hard for most teams to copy quickly.

entry.twist: It focuses only on running AI models fast and cheaply (not training them), and claims its chips are far more energy-efficient and cheaper than rivals like Nvidia.
entry.who_pays: Makers of robots, drones, cars, medical devices and security cameras buy the chips to add on-device AI.
entry.why_now: As AI moves into everyday devices, those devices need chips that can run AI without huge power use or cloud connections.
